talk: Vesting means you earn your shares over time instead of getting them all on day one. The usual deal is 4 years with a 1-year cliff: nothing until the first anniversary, then a quarter, then the rest month by month. It protects everyone if someone leaves early.

terms.meaning: The waiting period before any shares are earned.
Shares not earned yet. The company gets them back if you leave.

questions.prompt: A new head coach gets 48,000 shares, vesting over 4 years with a 1-year cliff. They leave after 10 months. How many shares have they earned?
working: Before the cliff, nothing is earned: 0 shares.
whyNot: That counts monthly vesting from day one: 4 x 12 = 48 months, and 48,000 / 48 x 10 = 10,000. The cliff means nothing vests in the first year until the anniversary.
48,000 / 4 = 12,000 is what vests at the 1-year cliff. They left 2 months short.
48,000 is the full grant, earned only after 4 years.

questions.prompt: Another coach with the same deal leaves after exactly 2 years. How many of their 48,000 shares have vested?
questions.hint: What share of the 4 years have they worked?
whyNot: 12,000 is just the cliff amount. Vesting carries on month by month after year one.

questions.prompt: Why do investors want founders on vesting too?
options: So a founder who leaves early doesn't keep a big stake for free
questions.hint: Think about a co-founder who quits in month 3.
working: If a co-founder quits early with a big stake, everyone still working carries a passenger.
Vesting means shares are earned by staying and building.
whyNot: Vesting doesn't change the valuation. It changes who earns the shares.
It's a contract term, not a law.
Vesting is about earning shares, not about tax.

penalty.prompt: A coach gets {grant} shares vesting over 4 years (48 months) with a 1-year cliff. They leave after {months} months. How many shares have vested?
penalty.hint: After the cliff, shares vest month by month over 48 months.
working: {months} months is past the 1-year cliff, so vesting counts from the start.

traps.why: That's only the cliff amount. Vesting continues month by month after year one.

call.title: Your co-founder wants out
call.prompt: Your co-founder owns 30% of the club and wants to leave after 8 months. There's no vesting agreement. Replacing them means giving a new hire 10% of the club, unless you get shares back to use.

options.label: Let them keep all 30%
options.result: They walk off with 30% for 8 months of work, and you hand over 10% more to hire their replacement.

options.label: Negotiate: they keep 5%, the rest comes back
options.result: Good call. 30% - 5% = 25% comes back, so you can hire the replacement without new dilution. $50,000 of legal fees is cheap next to 10% of the club. Next time, put everyone on vesting.

options.label: Hire a replacement on a bigger salary instead
options.result: $5,000 a matchday adds up fast, and they still keep 30% of the club for 8 months of work.

takeaway: Shares should be earned. 4 years with a 1-year cliff is the standard.
